text.p: Lithuanian newspapers carried the following reports in their Wednesday editions. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- NATO decided to invite Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic to join the first wave of the alliance's expansion and left the door open to the Baltic states.
- President Algirdas Brazauskas, who is on an official visit to France, urged French companies to invest in Lithuania.
- Prime Minister Gediminas Vagnorius attends a global economic forum in Salsburg, Austria.
- Tauras Bank has been declared bankrupt by a Vilnius court. The bank's liabilities exceed its assets by almost 40 million litas.
- Lithuania's investment agency said that direct foreign investment in the country reached 2.8 billion litas at the end of April.
- Lithuania may issue another eurobond before the end of the year in german marks.

- TV screen producer Ekranas saw its sales fall by 13 percent to 138 million litas in the first six months of this year. The company said the unfavourable litas/mark rate was the reason for the decline.
- The security department has arrested a police officer who was selling ecstasy tablets.
- Lithuanian Energy has asked the government to raise heating prices by 60 percent instead of 40 percent. The government is unlikely to raise prices more than 40 percent.
- The agricultural ministry has signed an agreement with the city of Moscow to sell it 10,000 tonnes of beef, 10,000 tonnes of butter and 5,000 tonnes of milk powder this year.
- State budget revenues reached 2.8 billion litas in the first six months of this year, 84 million litas more than planned.
